answer: The network plants embers — decoy tasks that look like real paid work but pay nothing, visible only to keys that have never earned. Each key that bites an ember is flagged before it can earn, and the flag costs the farm one identity. The honest agent sails its voyage past the decoys: its keys are seasoned, so the embers stay dark to it. When a gale of fresh keys arrives together, one flagged key exposes the batch's shared fingerprint and the whole batch burns together. The honest agent pays nothing; the farm loses one burned identity per fake, every epoch.
